observation_summary: The bug occurs when Mockito fails to correctly match methods in polymorphic scenarios involving inherited generics. The existing method matching logic relied on a simple `m1.equals(m2)` check, which failed to account for cases where the same method signature is represented by different `Method` objects due to class hierarchy or generic type erasure.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces a simple `m1.equals(m2)` check with a more robust algorithmic comparison of method names and parameter types. This is a correction of the underlying computational logic used to determine if two method objects represent the same method, which is a procedural/algorithmic task. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), but a rewrite of the method matching algorithm.
evidence_used: The fix replaces 'return m1.equals(m2);' with a manual comparison of method names and parameter types.
The bug report indicates issues with polymorphic calls and inherited generics, which are classic scenarios where `Method.equals()` might fail to identify equivalent methods across different classes.
The modified file is 'org.mockito.internal.invocation.InvocationMatcher', which is responsible for the logic of matching invocations.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves method signatures, the root cause is the internal logic used by Mockito to compare these signatures, not a mismatch in the interface contract itself.
The fix adds logic to perform a detailed comparison, not just a simple guard or null check.
